title: Measles has come raging back in the US. Robert F Kennedy Jr should be impeached | Judith Levine
text:
At least 11 Americans have died of measles since January 2025 – the month before Robert F Kennedy Jr became secretary of Health and Human Services.
One of Friday’s victims was a child, in Wisconsin, where a baby died of measles the week before. Pennsylvania has not disclosed the age of the other person.
Measles is a highly contagious but vaccine-preventable disease. It can kill you with pneumonia, leave you deaf, or permanently damage your immune system.
The disease was wiped out in the US a quarter-century ago. Yet in less than two years, outbreaks in 47 states have pushed the numbers of illnesses and deaths to levels unseen since 1991. The country has tallied more than 7,700 cases since January 2025, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
The majority of those sickened, hospitalized and killed by measles are under 20 years old; an alarming percentage are not yet five. In the past two years, 112 pregnant women have been hospitalized with complications of measles, until now extraordinarily rare. Two lost their pregnancies. A dozen babies have been born infected.
On 17 November, the Pan American Health Organization (Paho) revoked the US’s measles elimination status, which it has held since 2000.
Even before that, since the mid-1990s, only a few dozen to a few hundred cases were reported annually, and any small outbreaks were contained within the year, the standard for gaining and keeping the status. Now, says KFF Health News, “measles has re-established regular transmission in the country”.
The reason for this scourge is plain: a sliding vaccination rate. The reason for the slide is a growing suspicion of vaccines. That suspicion has been floating around for decades, but for its renewal and spread – as virulent as measles itself – we can thank the misinformation crusade led by the secretary of health and joined by the president.
Kennedy is a prolific conspiracy monger: wifi causes “leaky brain”; chemicals in the water turn children transgender. But his premier contribution to American stupidity has been to amplify the fiction that vaccinations cause autism.
Reuters called RFK Jr “the nation’s leading anti-vaccine activist”.
As the person responsible for safeguarding the health of the American people, Robert F Kennedy Jr is to blame for thousands of preventable cases of severe illness and at least 11 deaths. Almost to a person, these latter-day measles victims were unvaccinated.
Kennedy should be impeached.
Measles’ revival did not happen because the secretary of health was otherwise engaged, like so many of Trump’s incompetents. Rather, Kennedy seems almost deliberately to have invited fatal childhood diseases back into the US and nursed them to vitality.
The virus started spreading in Texas in January 2025, but the secretary has not mobilized the agency’s rumor-quelling mechanisms, or enlisted the help of the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), ordinarily the government’s partner in guiding frightened families through outbreaks.
If Kennedy has transmitted any messages, they’re mixed. He disputed being labeled as “anti-vaccine”, and endorsed the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccination as “effective”. Then he claimed it was “not safety tested”. (It is proven safe and effective.)
But in June 2025, in what he called “a bold step in restoring public trust” – and a long list of medical associations called the opposite – Kennedy fired all 17 members of the CDC Advisory Committee on Immunizations and packed the vaccine committee with vaccine skeptics. In January, following a presidential executive order full of pseudoscientific poppycock, the CDC released a plan to revise childhood immunization guidelines, both complicating and loosening them.
“At a time when parents, pediatricians and the public are looking for clear guidance and accurate information, this ill-considered decision will sow further chaos and confusion and erode confidence in immunizations,” the AAP president, Dr Andrew D Racine, said.
The AAP sued, and in March 2026 a federal judge annulled all votes taken by the reconstituted ACIP and ordered a restoration of the pre-Kennedy guidelines.
Nevertheless, Trump released another executive order this summer, debuting the anti-immunization committee’s “gold standard” recommendations. The president was keenest on breaking the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vax into separate shots. The three-in-one was “quite lethal”, he claimed, falsely. Experts say spacing out the immunizations would endanger children. Drugmakers suggest that the product can’t be sliced up anyway.
Kennedy has sown distrust in state health departments, long the source of data for the federal agencies. After Pennsylvania reported the deaths of two babies too young to be vaccinated, for instance, he posted without evidence that one of them “may … have been altogether fabricated”.
In September, the secretary ordered the CDC director, Erica Schwartz, to remove the two deaths from its publicly accessible data. In late October, Schwartz declined to sign off on an urgent health alert to clinicians encountering measles-related symptoms in pregnant patients that they have not seen in decades, or ever.
CDC higher-ups have inexplicably postponed other vaccine-related reports cleared for publication by expert readers. One was a study of infant mortality from whooping cough, or pertussis, which found that the mothers of most of the babies who died did not get a vaccine while pregnant that protects infants, who are most susceptible to severe pertussis.
Doctors were miffed. “We don’t have data on this part. The experience is limited,” a Canadian obstetrician told the Washington Post. “When I’m dealing with this situation, I’m dealing with not just Jane who’s pregnant, but the baby or babies inside her womb.”
The only conclusion to draw is that HHS doesn’t want us to know that vaccines save lives, and refusing them imperils lives, especially those of the most vulnerable.
After Paho withdrew the country’s measles elimination status this week, the CDC announced it would invest $100m to get it back: “We will encourage MMR vaccination, expand access to vaccines, and help communities close gaps in protection. We will equip state, local, tribal, and territorial health departments with tools and technical support to identify communities at increased risk, engage trusted partners, detect cases quickly, and respond effectively to outbreaks,” reads its statement.
It’s hard to imagine this plan represents an epiphany for the man who squandered a half-century of public health progress in the first place.
This week, the chair of an independent US advisory committee to the Paho betrayed his disgust. “We’ve gotten comfortable letting children be stopped by a deadly disease and die from it,” he said.
No, “we” have not. The Trump administration has. It is a cult high on “lethality” and blasé about death, whether in Pennsylvania or Ukraine, Wisconsin or Iran.
Kennedy is the cult’s guru. In Indianapolis in April 2025, when more than 800 Americans had already contracted measles and three had died, he praised his staff –and, by implication, his own leadership. The CDC, he said, had “done a very good job containing the measles outbreak”.
Trump is the cult’s No 1 apostle. But this is not the first time he has shrugged off the demise of the people he was elected to serve. During the Covid-19 epidemic, Axios asked the president to comment on the 1,000 people who were dying every day from suffocation and organ failure caused by the virus.
Replied Trump: “It is what it is.”
- Judith Levine is a frequent contributor to the Guardian. Her Substack is Today in Fascism
